item.title: Victoria Bateman: If every woman had the ability to control her own fertility, the world would be a very different place
item.description: The historian and Cambridge economist on the myths that erased women from history, the “tradwife” revival, and how control over women’s lives shapes economies.

item.title: Billy Bragg: If you don’t make a pitch for inclusivity around the space we call England, you leave it open to the far right
item.description: The punk legend on accountability, the dangers of cynicism, and protecting Englishness from the far right.

item.title: Antony Szmierek: Creativity feels magic to me, something powerful and frightening to the people who need to be frightened
item.description: The musician on sensitivity, censorship and why power always fears the arts.

item.title: Hamsa Yassin: My dream is that kids could name five trees before they can name five Kardashians
item.description: The wildlife cameraman, Strictly champion and children’s TV presenter on how modern life is squeezing the curiosity out of children too early.

item.title: James Murray MBE: The simplest and most powerful thing anyone can do is to take the story and pass it on
item.description: The actor, artist and campaigner on polluted rivers, the race to save wild salmon and why most activism should always begin with a story

item.title: Maria Alyokhina: Dictators will always do two things when they want more power – oppress women and ban jokes
item.description: The Russian political activist and Pussy Riot member on life under Putin, how repression works, and the cost of dissent in Russia.

item.title: Mary Portas: Every pound spent is a vote for the world you want
item.description: The businesswoman, broadcaster, author, and activist on community, consumerism and why buying less is the most radical choice we have.

item.title: Oyinkan Braithwaite: After food and shelter, the next essential thing a child should receive is access to books
item.description: The Nigerian-British novelist and writer on growing up between Lagos and London, the loss of community in the UK, and why societies only change when children are taught to imagine lives beyond their own.

item.title: Hollie McNish: We pretend we’re free, but we follow rules we never chose
item.description: The poet and author on why more us should interrogate things society tells us are normal.

item.title: Ny Oh: A quiet voice repeating the same thing over a long period of time is far more powerful than loud voices that run out of steam
item.description: The UK-born, New Zealand-raised, musician who toured with Harry Styles on why playing to three people in a forest is more meaningful than playing to a crowd of thousands.
